title: The sharp support–concentration bound for subset sums
decision_reason: Explicit original formulation and independently authored current corroboration, fresh status and duplicate checks, ten formal scope comparisons, separated A58 self-review and technical validation passed. No matching unresolved resolution claim located.
aliases: Anticoncentration versus the number of subset sums
Weighted Bernoulli sum support versus maximum atom
H0 <= 2 H-infinity for weighted fair Bernoulli sums

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Every integer n>=1 and every fixed real vector w=(w_1,...,w_n), allowing repeated, negative and zero coordinates.
problem_fingerprint.randomness: X_1,...,X_n are independent Bernoulli(1/2); all 2^n labelled subsets have equal probability.
problem_fingerprint.observable: S_w=sum_i w_i X_i; R(w)={sum_i w_i x_i:x in {0,1}^n}; N(w)=|R(w)|; rho(w)=max_t Pr[S_w=t]. Distinct exact real totals and point probabilities, with no tolerance or modular arithmetic.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: N(w) rho(w)^2 <= 1 for every such n,w. Equivalently N(w)<=rho(w)^(-2). No asymptotic slack or unspecified multiplicative prefactor.
problem_fingerprint.counting_equivalence: M(w)=max_t |{x in {0,1}^n:sum_i w_i x_i=t}|=2^n rho(w); target N(w)M(w)^2<=4^n.
problem_fingerprint.entropy_equivalence: H_0(S_w)=log N(w), H_infinity(S_w)=-log rho(w) with the same logarithm base; target H_0<=2H_infinity.
problem_fingerprint.degenerate_case: If all weights are zero, N=rho=1 and both entropies vanish.
problem_fingerprint.sharpness: Exponent 2 cannot be uniformly decreased: all-one weights give N=n+1 and rho=2^(-n) binomial(n,floor(n/2)); log N/(-log rho) tends to 2.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model: A mathematical inequality, with no algorithmic running-time conclusion in its assertion.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One family, including real/integer, counting/probability/entropy formulations; no extra counts for parameter choices or restricted weights.

issues_resolved: Retained M=2^n rho, exact real support, all-zero convention, exponent sharpness and fair-bit quantifiers.
Read both entropy theorem statements and Section 3 interpolation; retained the input-dependent logarithmic term and recorded why alpha tending to zero does not give two.

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: For epsilon>0, n>=epsilon^(-1/2) and real w with rho(w)>=exp(-epsilon n), N(w)<=exp(C sqrt(epsilon) n), C absolute.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: This leaves sqrt(epsilon) instead of the conjectural exact 2 epsilon dependence. The conjecture paragraph is distinct from the proved equation (1.2).

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: For 0<alpha<1, H_alpha<=C_alpha H_infinity. For alpha>=1/2 the constant is 2; for alpha<1/2 it is [k_alpha+2(1-2^(k_alpha) alpha)]/(1-alpha), k_alpha=ceil(log_2(1/(2alpha))).
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: C_alpha diverges as alpha decreases to zero. Taking the zero-order limit therefore does not produce factor two. Monotonicity has H_0>=H_alpha, so the positive-order bound cannot be substituted for H_0.

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: For nonzero real w and m nonzero coordinates, H_0<=min{log_2(m+1),2+log_2(m log(2)/H_infinity)} H_infinity, with natural logarithms in the entropies.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Input-dependent coefficient; the zero vector is treated separately. The proof’s interpolation keeps an alpha m log(2) term and does not remove the logarithmic loss. Separated repeated blocks scale m and H_infinity together, so repetition alone does not drive this coefficient down to two.

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: A multiplicity beta>=2^((1-epsilon)n) forces support N<=2^(delta(epsilon)n), with delta=O(log log(1/epsilon)/sqrt(log(1/epsilon))) as epsilon decreases to zero.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Normalize rho=beta/2^n. This qualitative tradeoff does not reach the exact target; the updated introduction records the improved JSS bound. Lemma 3.5 justifies the application, not the conjecture.

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: For every epsilon>0 some integer n and w in Z^n have N(w)>2^((1-epsilon)n) and M(w)>2^(0.2563 n).
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The two lower bounds only force N M^2 above 2^((1.5126-epsilon)n), not above 4^n. The stated construction theorem is not a refutation of the present inequality. This assessment does not assert a separately proved upper bound for every vector in its construction.

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: For a prime p and a set S of distinct residues, uniform m-subsets satisfy point bounds 1/p+C/(|S| sqrt(m)) for C log|S|<=m<=10^(-3)|S|/log|S|. Corollary 1.4 covers 1<=m<=(1-epsilon)|S| with a sqrt(log|S|) loss.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Corollary 1.4 includes central sizes, so the theorem is not dismissed merely by Theorem 1.3’s range. Both sample without replacement from distinct group elements and bound in |S|, not the full support N(w). Even an embedding without wraparound does not supply the sharp N(w)^(-1/2) bound or handle repeated weights automatically.

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: Fix T,L>=1 and epsilon,nu in (0,1). For a set A of n>=2 elements of Z_Q, Q=tq, t<=T, gcd(t,q)=1, Omega(q)<=L, either at least (1-nu)n elements lie in a proper q-large subgroup coset or every uniform m-subset, 1<=m<=(1-epsilon)n, has point probability <=1/Q+C sqrt(log(2+n))/(n sqrt(m)). Omega counts prime factors with multiplicity; q-large means subgroup order divisible by a prime factor of q.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The alternative is a structural conclusion for a distinct-element set in a bounded-prime-factor cyclic group. Its probability bound depends on input cardinality, with a loss and constants, rather than arbitrary weighted real support. No stated recursion gives the present sharp inequality. The conditioned-chain result also retains these model restrictions.

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: For positive n-element sets, classify support <=binomial(n+1,2)+1+M when n>=4, 0<=M<=n-4. More generally support <=C n^2 implies a lattice bulk with total O_C(n^2) and O_C(1) exceptional elements. Theorem 1.3 gives support >=gamma_d(epsilon)n^(d+1) under a proper-subspace occupancy bound.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: These are conditional small-support structure results and support lower bounds. They do not conclude N rho^2<=1 for all support sizes or multisets. The paper’s real/torsion-free extension and its explicit Littlewood–Offord discussion were checked, rather than excluding it solely for positive weights.

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: For each fixed integer C>=-1 and n>=N_C, positive n-element sets with support <=T_n+n+C+1 are exactly dilates of primitive integer sets of total <=T_n+n+C or exceptional E_n(m,pi), m in {1,2}, pi of weight C+m or C+m+1. T_n=binomial(n+1,2). E_n is the stated initial integer interval with m removed and partition-displaced final elements.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The September 14 sequel covers all fixed defects, beyond the earlier two boundaries. It still assumes distinct positive elements, support close to its quadratic minimum, and a threshold depending on the fixed defect. Choosing a defect depending on an arbitrary input does not establish the required n>=N_C or a bound on its largest atom.

resolution_comparisons.formal_scope: For a finite abelian group G of order n, count all h-element subsets of G with each group-valued sum. As n tends to infinity, the minimum count divided by the maximum tends to one for 4<=h<=floor(n/2)+1; complement symmetry extends the range in Wang.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The ground population is the entire finite group, each element once, with fixed subset size and an asymptotic conclusion. This is different from arbitrary repeated real weights, independent fair selections and an exact bound at every finite n. Hu supplies a shorter proof of this group theorem, not a new general entropy comparison.

independently_authored_corroboration.assessment: Jiange Li shares no authors with Jain–Sah–Sawhney and explicitly states the same all-real-weight, fair-bit inequality in September 2026. This is a separate scholarly work, not another version of the original paper. The author attributes its communication to Mokshay Madiman.

nearest_existing.distinction: A bounded-word computational lower bound for finding three distinct elements satisfying an additive equation. No support-versus-largest-atom inequality is asserted.
A comparison of integer and fractional cutting-stock optima, with exact ceiling-plus-one gap. Shared packing relevance does not identify its assertion with a subset-sum entropy bound.
The best asymptotic competitive ratio of deterministic online packing. Its unknown-arrival decision model and objective differ from this inequality for fixed input weights.

normalization_checks: All finite n>=1 and real weights; repeated, zero and negative coordinates retained. Indices distinguish equal-weight items.
Exactly fair independent bits. Already for one nonzero weight with bias p close to zero, support 2 and maximum probability close to one violate the proposed extension to arbitrary biases.
N counts distinct exact values, not subsets or approximate bins. M counts subsets; M=2^n rho, so N M^2<=4^n is the correct translation.
The target entropy factor is independent of a common logarithm base. The public partial-bound expression uses natural entropies and m log(2) exactly as in Li.
The all-zero case satisfies the main bound and is excluded only from the partial formula containing division by H_infinity.
For all-one weights, Stirling’s formula gives rho of order n^(-1/2); log(n+1)/(-log rho) tends to 2. Sharpness concerns the exponent, not nontrivial equality for every n.

Deleting zero weights leaves the probability law unchanged. Flipping a negative weight amounts to replacing its fair bit by its complement and translating the sum; this does not justify deleting repetitions or perturbing collisions.
The unconditional law is a binomial mixture of fixed-size subset laws. Conditioning alone does not convert the inspected group bounds into the target bound in total support.
No separate candidate or active ID for the entropy, counting, integer, sign-normalized or dimension-restricted formulations.
scope_normalization: The finite all-real-weight statement follows Li Conjecture 1.1 and the exact linear conjecture preceding JSS equation (1.2). All models and formula conversions are explicit. No biased-bit or interval-concentration strengthening is introduced.
